title: Misinformation and polarization in the 2023 elections in Spain: a study of Vox on Instagram (Desinformación y polarización en las elecciones de España 2023: un estudio de Vox en Instagram)
screen_reason: Quantitative content analysis of all 109 videos posted by the Spanish party Vox on its official Instagram account in the month before the 23 July 2023 general election, with two coders, a codebook and Cohen's kappa = 0.86. It reports a share of items judged to contain disinformation against an external typology (Wardle 2017): 65% of the videos contain some kind of information disorder. That is a CONTENT prevalence share with a stated denominator.

estimates.measure_type: % of videos posted by Vox's official Instagram account that contain some type of disinformation (any of Wardle's seven information-disorder levels)
estimates.value_raw: 65% de los videos publicados por Vox en Instagram contiene algún tipo de desinformación, mientras el 35% no presenta ningún desorden informativo (n=109)
estimates.denominator: 109 videos (all audiovisual posts) published on Vox's official Instagram account @vox_es between 23 June and 22 July 2023; static image posts were excluded from the sample
estimates.definition: A video was counted if coders identified in it any of the seven levels of information disorder in Wardle's (2017) typology: satire or parody, false connection, misleading content, false context, imposter content, manipulated content, or fabricated content
estimates.misinfo_def: 'Independientemente de las múltiples definiciones que giran en torno al concepto de desinformación, su fin último es obtener algún tipo de beneficio mediante el engaño y la confusión que genera en la ciudadanía' [Whatever the many definitions of disinformation, its ultimate aim is to obtain some kind of benefit through the deception and confusion it generates among citizens]; operationalised with Wardle's (2017) seven-level typology
estimates.source_quote: Los resultados apuntan a que el 65% de los videos publicados por Vox en Instagram contiene algún tipo de desinformación, mientras el 35% no presenta ningún desorden informativo (Gráfico 1).
estimates.page_loc: Section 4.2 'Niveles de desinformación en los contenidos de Vox', p.195; Gráfico 1
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two coders applied a purpose-built codebook operationalising Wardle's (2017) seven-level disinformation typology; a 10% pretest was run 23-28 October 2023 and full data collection 1 November - 11 December 2023; inter-coder reliability Cohen's kappa = 0.86. No external fact-checker was used
estimates.notes: English translation of the source quote: 'The results indicate that 65% of the videos published by Vox on Instagram contain some type of disinformation, while 35% show no information disorder.' Note the very broad numerator: it includes satire/parody, which the authors themselves call the lowest level and say is not intended to disinform, so breadth is coded 'misleading' (the broadest band). The census is one party's own output on one account in one campaign month, hence denom_selection=single_source and population_scope=elite_politician; this is not a platform-level or news-diet prevalence. Arithmetic check: Table 2's type percentages imply a disinformation subset of 70 videos, and 70/109 = 64.2%, so the reported 65% is a light rounding; the verbatim 65% is kept per R8. The text at section 4.1 says 'Los 10 videos publicados por Vox' which is an evident typo for 109.
estimates.moderator_quote: Siguiendo estos criterios de selección, la muestra está compuesta por 109 contenidos audiovisuales (n=109). [...] Conviene mencionar que en la realización del análisis de contenido se utilizó el índice de fiabilidad interjueces, de tal manera que el coeficiente de la Kappa (k) de Cohen es de 0,86, lo cual dota de una muy buena fiabilidad entre los codificadores

estimates.measure_type: % of the disinformative Vox videos whose disinformation was of the strictest type, 'fabricated content' (content created solely in order to deceive)
estimates.denominator: The subset of Vox Instagram videos already coded as containing disinformation (the seven type percentages in Table 2 sum to 100%, implying roughly 70 of the 109 videos); the subset size is never stated verbatim
estimates.definition: Video coded at Wardle's highest level, 'contenido fabricado': material 'que se crean de manera intencionada y exclusiva para engañar' [created intentionally and exclusively in order to deceive]
estimates.misinfo_def: 'el contenido fabricado representa el nivel más alto de desinformación y corresponde a aquellos materiales que se crean de manera intencionada y exclusiva para engañar' [fabricated content is the highest level of disinformation and corresponds to material created intentionally and exclusively in order to deceive]
estimates.source_quote: A continuación, aparece el contenido fabricado (18,6%), seguido de la sátira (8,6%) y del contenido impostor (5,7%). Por último, se encuentra el contenido manipulado (2,9%).
estimates.page_loc: Section 4.2, p.196; Tabla 2 'Niveles de desinformación en los videos de Vox'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Same two-coder procedure and codebook as the headline row; Cohen's kappa = 0.86 for the content analysis overall
estimates.notes: APPENDIX-ONLY row under R3: this percentage is computed inside the disinformation-only subset, not over the 109-video sample, because Table 2's seven type shares sum to exactly 100%. The prose ('identificados respectivamente en el 21,4% de los videos') reads as if it were a share of all videos, which is the ambiguity flagged here; the summing-to-100% table settles it in favour of the misinformation-only denominator, and the subset size (~70) is inferred, not stated. Do NOT combine with the 65% row to derive a fabricated share of all videos - that would be a computed product, which R8 forbids. Included so an adjudicator can see the strictest-breadth reading the paper supports; drop it if the review does not carry within-misinfo composition rows.
estimates.moderator_quote: Respecto al nivel de desinformación, los datos revelan que los tipos de contenidos desinformativos predominantes en las publicaciones de Vox son: conexión falsa, contenido engañoso y contexto falso, identificados respectivamente en el 21,4% de los videos (véase Tabla 2).

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) the remaining six Wardle type shares in Table 2 (satire 8.6%, false connection 21.4%, misleading content 21.4%, false context 21.4%, imposter 5.7%, manipulated 2.9%) - same within-misinfo denominator as the fabricated row, omitted per R4 (quality over quantity) since one within-misinfo composition row already documents the pattern; (b) polarization results (negative 59%, positive 25%, neutral 16%) and the emotion distribution (anger 43%, joy 27%, disgust 15%, fear 8%, sadness 4%, surprise 3%) - these are tone/affect codings, not veracity, so they are not a misinformation construct; (c) Santiago Abascal appearing as the main figure in 86.2% of the sample - an actor-presence share, not a misinformation share; (d) audience figures (mean 23,389 likes and 760 comments per video; 2,549,417 likes and 82,840 comments in total) - engagement counts with no misinformation numerator, and no exposure denominator, so no EXPOSURE or REACH row is derivable. No CONCENTRATION row is possible: nothing links a top group of sources or users to a share of exposure or sharing.

rob.design: Exploratory single-account content analysis. Sampling frame is a full census of the 109 videos posted on Vox's official Instagram account (@vox_es, 718k followers) between 23 June and 22 July 2023, the month before the 23 July general election; static image posts were deliberately excluded, so the denominator is videos only and not all party output. Coding by two coders against a written codebook operationalising Wardle's (2017) seven-level typology, with a 10% pretest (23-28 October 2023) preceding full coding (1 November - 11 December 2023); inter-coder reliability reported as Cohen's kappa = 0.86. No response rate applies. Weaknesses: the disinformation judgement is researcher-made with no external fact-check benchmark, satire is folded into the disinformation numerator, the number of videos in the disinformation subset is never stated, and section 4.1 contains an internal inconsistency ('Los 10 videos publicados por Vox' where 109 is meant).
rob.item6_quote: Considerando lo anterior, este artículo considera la siguiente tipología de desinformación, basada en siete categorías y una escala que va desde la menor hasta la mayor intencionalidad de engañar (Wardle, 2017): 1) Sátira o parodia; 2) Conexión falsa; 3) Contenido engañoso; 4) Contexto falso; 5) Contenido impostor; 6) Contenido manipulado; y 7) Contenido fabricado. [Taking the above into account, this article uses the following typology of disinformation, based on seven categories on a scale running from lowest to highest intent to deceive (Wardle, 2017): 1) Satire or parody; 2) False connection; 3) Misleading content; 4) False context; 5) Imposter content; 6) Manipulated content; and 7) Fabricated content.]
